fixes.explanation: A little sin here and there can sound reasonable, friend. But Paul doesn't leave room for an "at times." He says "Certainly not!" (Romans 6:15). That's the whole answer.

I get the pick, baker, but Paul doesn't offer a third option. He says you're a slave either "…to sin leading to death, or to obedience leading to righteousness." (Romans 6:16). Two choices are on the table, and there's no third door.
Not quite, friend. Paul says "…slaves to sin leading to death…" (Romans 6:16). Freedom isn't where that master leads. Death is the destination he names.

Paul doesn't limit it to parts never used for sin, friend. He says, "Just as you used to offer the parts of your body in slavery to impurity… so now offer them in slavery to righteousness" (Romans 6:19). The very parts that once served impurity now get a new master.

Proud isn't the word Paul uses, friend. He calls them "…the things of which you are now ashamed?" (Romans 6:21). The word now matters, because it's how they look back on those things today. Shame is the feeling Paul names.

Yes, baker! "…the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord." (Romans 6:23). Wages are what you earn, but a gift is handed to you. Paul wants us to see that difference clearly. Eternal life comes in Christ Jesus our Lord.
